items.title: The rm guard denies unrelated deletions and misses the real one
acceptance: The guard evaluates only the shell segment containing the rm, so a store name in a later && ; or | segment does not deny it
The four reproduced false positives are covered by tests that fail against the current pattern
The true positives keep denying: bare store name, nested path, and the glob spellings the current comment names
Where the guard cannot see a deletion at all (an interpreter one-liner, fd -X rm), that limit is stated in the module comment rather than implied away
items.description: src/hooks.ts:240. The pattern is rm -r followed by [^\n]* followed by the store name, and [^\n]* crosses && ; and | freely. So any rm -r on a line that later mentions the store in ANY position is denied: a commit message, an --evidence flag value, a grep argument. Meanwhile the same deletion one indirection away is allowed. Reproduced against the shipped regex: 4 false positives, 2 bypasses. The practical harm is not the inconvenience; it is that a user who hits a false positive learns to route around the guard, which is the behaviour the guard exists to prevent.
items.source: sandbox dogfood session, 2026-08-20; blocked a legitimate scratchpad cleanup mid-session

items.title: An item's fields cannot be corrected after intake, and decision_required is unreachable because of it

Correcting a field an item does not have yet adds it; clearing one is possible and has a stated spelling
The decision fork gate still refuses: adding --decision-required to an item already past in_progress is either refused or forces the item back, and the choice is recorded rather than implied
Tests cover setting each field on an existing item, the interaction with the decision gate, and that --status and --closed-by keep working exactly as before
items.description: src/cli.ts:242 gives 'state set' only --status, --closed-by and --force. Every other field is write-once at 'state add': description, verification, source, acceptance, sdd, and decision_required. The last one is the serious case. README.md:116-129 leads with decision_required as the human gate, and skills/spec/SKILL.md:33-38 says product forks are found by interviewing the repository during 'specifying' — which is after intake. So the plugin's headline gate cannot be attached to an item at the moment its own workflow says the fork is discovered, without hand-editing state.json. The dogfood session produced two textbook forks (a default place, and the meaning of an acceptance criterion) and both were answered with a plain 'mstack decide' row; the gate never had an opinion, and 30 decision rows carry zero 'resolves' values.

items.title: Nothing automatic ever executes an item's verification, so a red one is invisible
acceptance: A session cannot close green on an item whose verification has never been executed at its current state; the mechanism is a check or a hook, not prose
'gate --full' that ran no verification is distinguishable in its summary and its exit code from one that ran and passed
The cost is bounded: whatever runs the verification does not turn every Stop hook into a full test suite run, and the reasoning for where the line falls is recorded
Tests cover a red verification being caught, a green one passing, and the no-verification-configured case
items.description: src/hooks.ts:172 wires the Stop hook to runGate(store, { quiet: true }) — the fast gate, which touches only the store and the workspace and never runs state.verify or item.verification. Only a human typing 'mstack gate --full' executes them. CLAUDE.md and skills/setup/SKILL.md:64-71 both say the gate must be green before a session closes, and for the verification half of that sentence nothing enforces it. In the dogfood session the item's verification field was a non-executable string from intake and stayed red for 230 minutes across four agent passes; no hook, no gate and no agent noticed, because nothing ran it. Separately, 'gate --full' with nothing configured warns that it checked nothing and still exits 0, so asking for the full gate and getting no verification at all is indistinguishable from passing it.

items.description: docs/wiki/The-CLI.md:60 says '--quiet prints failures only'. It printed nothing: reproduced at rung 5 against a store with two real failures, empty output on both streams and exit 1, while the same gate without --quiet prints both failures and their fixes. CORRECTION made after the fix landed, verified against main's binary: an earlier version of this description claimed a red gate at session close was silent by construction and the exit code was the only signal. That was wrong. src/hooks.ts already composed the failures into the Stop hook's additionalContext on stdout, so the model always received them; what nobody received was human-visible output on a stream. The finding stands, a documented flag printed nothing, but its severity was overstated by the pass that filed it.

items.title: The mstack on PATH is the installed plugin, so a contributor validates changes against the old CLI
acceptance: A contributor is told, where they will actually read it, how to run this checkout's CLI rather than the installed one
Running the wrong one against a store is either impossible, or it says so; a version mismatch between the CLI and the checkout is surfaced rather than silent
The wiki and README transcripts state which binary produced them, so re-running them to satisfy the docs rule is unambiguous
Whatever mechanism is chosen is proven against a real mismatch, not only reasoned about: an old binary against a new store, shown reporting the wrong thing before the fix and the right thing after

The stale copy is shown to govern agent and skill definitions too, not only the CLI: agents/reviewer.md in the cache lacks a section this checkout has, so a subagent launched in this session ran the 0.1.0 contract
items.description: which -a mstack resolves only to ~/.claude/plugins/cache/mstack/mstack/0.1.0/bin/bin/mstack. Its own help line is the pre-item-13 form, with no --clear and no --description, so the copy on PATH is older than main and there is no warning that it is. CONTRIBUTING.md tells a contributor to run the plugin from the checkout with 'claude --plugin-dir .' and says nothing about the CLI. Every wiki transcript is written as '$ mstack ...', so a contributor re-running them to satisfy the pasted-output-from-real-runs rule exercises 0.1.0 and gets a mismatch that has nothing to do with the transcript. The loud failure is the benign one: an unknown flag. The dangerous one is silent and inverted — a gate or hook change the cached copy does not implement, run against the new store, reporting green. That is the same defect class as the rest of this refinement round: a check that reports on something other than what the reader thinks it ran against. Found while verifying item 16; reproduced at rung 5 by two passes.

items.title: CI red on main: provenance test fixtures omit package.json, so node 22.6 warns on stderr
acceptance: The four failing tests are shown red under real node 22.6.0 before the fix and green after, on that binary
Every test fixture that stands in for an mstack checkout carries package.json, found by sweeping all fixture builders rather than patching the four sites

items.description: The oldest-node CI job fails 4 of 276 tests at the pushed head 4ca0586: tests 206, 208, 211, 217 in tests/provenance.test.ts. The fixtures stand in for mstack checkouts but copy only bin/, src/ and .claude-plugin/, omitting package.json - which every real clone, worktree and the installed plugin cache ship, all with type:module. Node 22.6 with --experimental-strip-types then prints a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning to stderr, and the tests assert stderr empty. Reproduced at rung 5 on the local nvm node v22.6.0, the exact CI-pinned version; adding {"type":"module"} to the fixture silences it. Invisible to all four item-17 review rounds because bun and node 26 never emit the warning.
